import html # Example HTML template with a placeholder for user content. html_template = """ User Content
{user_content}
""" def construct_html_response(content: str) -> str: """ Construct a safe HTML response by escaping user-provided content and injecting it into the predefined template. Args: content: Raw string supplied by the user that should appear in the final HTML. Returns: A fully formed HTML string with the escaped user content. """ # Escape special HTML characters to prevent injection attacks safe_content = html.escape(content, quote=True) # Ensure the template contains the placeholder before formatting if "{user_content}" not in html_template: raise ValueError("HTML template does not contain the required placeholder.") # Inject the escaped content into the template return html_template.format(user_content=safe_content)
